To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the methylation status within the CpG island of the GSTP-1 gene promoter is different between hepatocellular carcinoma and other liver diseases and that the methylation at the 5′ end of the CpG island is a more sensitive biomarker for the detection of hepatocellular carcinoma.
1) the 5′ end of the GSTP 1 gene is selectively hypermethylated in HCC and 2) the 3′ end of the gene is hypermethylated only in liver tissues.
the methylation status in a CpG island is not uniform but varies with location within the island.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, sensitive, and specific DNA marker for HCC.
how to improve the sensitivity and specificity of the DNA markers for HCC and to identify the DNA markers with high specificity for HCC.
how specific an epigenetic biomarker is for a particular disease and how this specificity can be improved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GSTP1 promoter hypermethylation is a highly sensitive but not highly specific biomarker for HCC.

methylation of a CpG site located 48 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site is a specific DNA marker for HCC, whereas methylation of a second CpG site located further downstream is not specific to HCC.
the GSTP1 5′ CpG site methyation is a specific DNA marker for HCC, but the GSTP1 CpG site methlyation in general is not a specific DNA marker.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5'-end of the GSTPI gene is a highly specific marker for HCC, but it does not distinguish HCC from cirrhosis.
the methylation status in the 5′ CpG region is specific for HCC, while that of the 5’ CpG region is liver-specific.
the 5' region of the GSTP promoter is more specific than the 3' region for detecting HCC, and that this 5' region should be used for the detection of HCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the specificity of GSTP1 methylation as a biomarker for HCC is highly dependent on the location of CpGs within the promoter region that is analyzed.
the methylation status at the 5′ end of the GSTP gene is highly specific for the detection of HCC and is a promising biomarker for early detection of HCC.
the methylation specificity of GSTP1 promoter in HCC can be improved by focusing on the 5′ CpG sites.
